title: Outside services' issues: identify them, stop calling, ask for help (and overpass-api.de off)
why: Jason, 2026-11-14: an API with an issue is identified, the system stops trying it until it's resolved, and asks for help with the exact issue while the rest keeps working. New app/lib/ServiceHealth.php: each failure from an outside service is classified (refused us 403/406, key refused 401, quota, slow down 429, no answer, 5xx, unreadable) with its evidence (status, what it said, when, the crawler or the site). A ban, a refused key or a used-up quota holds every call to that server until a person marks it resolved or its light probe (Overpass /api/status, once a day, with exactly the agent that was refused) says it's lifted; slow-downs, timeouts and server errors back off 10 minutes doubling to 6 hours and clear on the next answer. One Pulse case per issue (svc:<id>) names it with its evidence and links (the OSM statement, the forum, FOSSGIS; each service's console), with Check it now and Mark resolved; the service's card shows it too. The crawler service sends the holds, due probes and the month's OpenStreetMap asks with each plan, and files the worker's issues, probes and asks from each report; a task held by a service reports Held, never Failed, so the run isn't a failure on Railway. The site's own Overpass calls (OpenPlaces, DeepLook) drop overpass-api.de, skip a held server, go one at a time, record failures, and keep a spot and kind 30 days (was 7). Migration 2026-11-14_service_issues (service_issues, crawl_osm_asks; seeds the known overpass-api.de ban, so the first run probes its status once). Worker 2.5 (merged after this is live): the same classification and holds for every API it calls, no GET retry after a 406, overpass-api.de off its list, one small query per kind, one at a time, 30-day cache per town and kind, a contact in the User-Agent (CRAWLER_CONTACT).

items: No new fatal errors in the logs

log.msg: Plan approved (no switch: everyone at once when published), advancing on schedule.
Put on staging (8 files); its checks passed.
